The Nernst effect, a thermoelectric conversion mech-
anism that transforms thermal gradients into transverse
electrical signals, holds significant promise for applica-
tions in waste heat recovery and highly sensitive thermal
sensors [1–6]. In conventional ferromagnetic systems, the
anomalous Nernst thermopower (SxAy) empirically scales
with the magnetization SxAy = QSµ0M, in which QS is
anomalous Nernst coefficient and ranges from 0.05 to
1 µVK−1T−1 for trivial ferromagnets. Recent explo-
rations of magnetic topological quantum materials have
revealed that their non-zero Berry curvature can generate
a giant anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) [7–14].
The Nernst thermopower is expressed as [15],

In our prior work, we observed a large Berry
curvature-driven room-temperature anomalous Nernst
thermopower (4.6 µV/K at 300 K) in LaCo5 single
crystals—a kagome and honeycomb magnet with a high
Curie temperature (TC = 840 K) [26, 27]. First-principles
calculations revealed a dense distribution of Weyl points
near the Fermi level, suggesting a strong Berry curva-
ture contribution [26]. To further optimize the ANE, in
this work, we engineered Pr-doped LaCo5 (La1−xPrxCo5,
x = 0.09, 0.21, 0.45) by introducing chemical pressure via
partial Pr-for-La substitution. Crucially, this strategy

The anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC), calculated via
σxAy ≈ ρAyx/ρ2xx, reveals critical doping effects: at 10
K, La0.91Pr0.09Co5 achieves σxAy ≈ 635 Ω−1cm−1, ex-
ceeding both the La0.55Pr0.45Co5 (∼375 Ω−1cm−1) and
La0.79Pr0.21Co5 (∼535 Ω−1cm−1). Room-temperature
σxAy values converge to ∼145 Ω−1cm−1 for both x =
0.21 and 0.45 systems—a 3 times enhancement over
LaCo5 (∼50 Ω−1cm−1). In La0.91Pr0.09Co5, the room-
temperature AHC is about 110 Ω−1cm−1. Given the
large number of Weyl points near the Fermi energy in
the parent material LaCo5, the variation in AHC could
be attributed to the shift in the Fermi energy induced by
Pr doping, which alters the Berry curvature integral over
the entire Brillouin zone [26].

cation suggested by the AHC evolution under Pr doping,
we conducted systematic ANE measurements—a critical
